title: Josh Allen is highest-ranked QB in NFL’s Top 100 Players list
description: Allen has been named the No. 1 QB on this player-voted list
fullText:
Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has officially been ranked as the highest quarterback, according to the annual NFL Top 100 list.

Last week, Allen was among the five players left to be ranked after the league hit Number 95. The others: Matthew Stafford, the only other quarterback left on the list, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Miles Garrett, and Bijan Robinson.

The five remaining players in this year's NFL Top 100:

🔵 Josh Allen
🟡 Myles Garrett
🔴 Bijan Robinson
🟢 Jaxon Smith-Njigba
🟡 Matthew Stafford

Agree or disagree that these are the five best players in the league? pic.twitter.com/MyOMsSxMH9

On Monday, wide receiver Smith-Njigba got the nod. This morning it was Matthew Stafford listed at number four:

No. 4 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026…@RamsNFL QB Matthew Stafford! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/5MUoVrcCcS

That leaves Allen as the only quarterback left on the list.

Allen finished the 2025 season with 3668 yards and 25 touchdowns. His 102.2 passer rating was fifth best in the NFL – behind Lamar Jackson (103.8), Jared Goff (105.5), Matthew Stafford (109.2), and Drake Maye (113.5).

While many thought Maye should get the NFL's MVP honor, that went to Stafford. Now, Allen has beaten them both out for the NFL's final 2025 honor. Instead of talking heads making the decisions, players are. And we can assume, this means that NFL players fear Allen much more than Maye who finished at 11.

Remember, before the 2024 season, an ESPN article that surveyed 100-plus players listed Allen as the most overrated quarterback. He proceeded to win the NFL MVP that season. Last year, Allen was listed at No. 3 on this very list.

While we await his final placement, Bills fans can laud, taunt, relish, or however you choose to celebrate (aka rubbing it in to those rivals to our east), the fact that the best quarterback in the league plays in Buffalo.

title: Tua Tagovailoa caught in Instagram faux pas
description: It has been a rough time for Tua Tagovailoa in recent years and he needs all the public support he can get, even if it comes from himself. The Miami Dolphins cut Tua following the 2025 season after seeing a precipitous drop in form and struggles with injuries. In doing so, they ate an NFL-record…
fullText:
It has been a rough time for Tua Tagovailoa in recent years and he needs all the public support he can get, even if it comes from himself.

The Miami Dolphins cut Tua following the 2025 season after seeing a precipitous drop in form and struggles with injuries. In doing so, they ate an NFL-record $99.2 million in dead cap space to move on and start over.

Tagovailoa was able to find a new home with the Atlanta Falcons where he is competing with former first round draft pick Michael Penix Jr. for the starting job. While the Falcons haven't won the NFC South since 2016, some decent quarterback play to go along with their exciting skill position players could provide some serious competition in an open division.

However, that quarterback play has remained a huge question mark. And after neither quarterback won the job during the preseason, the Falcons have yet to name a starter with the regular season just a week away.

However, Tua Tagovailoa is at least still trying to win Falcons fans over, although his recent post on Instagram was the equivalent of a social media pick six.

Tagovailoa posted a picture of himself in a Falcons uniform with the caption "For the A." That is obviously not a story. However, the first comment underneath the post was himself commenting "We're so proud of you! You got this!" with a heart emoji. The comment was screenshotted and shared several times before it was finally deleted.

Tua forgot to switch to his burner pic.twitter.com/SrznFjLYJA

— Austin Latham (@AustinLatham25) September 1, 2026

It's easy to see this, point and laugh, and assume some kind of wider Kevin Durant burner activity that is ongoing where Tua Tagovailoa is scrolling the internet trying to silence critics and hype up his chances of winning the Falcons starting quarterback job. Of course, a much more logical explanation is that whoever is managing his social media accounts forgot to log back into his or her personal account before leaving the supporting message.

Still though, as innocuous as the truth probably is, it still stands as a symbol of Tua's fall down the NFL pecking order at quarterback. And the fact that he needs all the help and hope he can get in getting his career back on track.

title: Charlie Baker: When NFL, NBA players return to campus, everyone else pays the price
description: All four Power Conferences have signed off on the Protect College Sports Act. NCAA President Charlie Baker writes why it must be passed into law.
fullText:
The notion college sports are for college students who will move on when they complete their degree or turn pro enjoys near-universal support. But right now, that fundamental boundary is being dismantled amid a relentless wave of litigation.

In two cases, the NCAA has been ordered to allow professional basketball players to return to college basketball, despite the fact they intentionally left college to go to the NBA Draft and each played in several NBA games. In another case, a judge required the NCAA to allow an athlete to compete for a fifth school in five years. And in the past two weeks, without so much as a hearing, let alone a trial, two courts permitted NFL players to return immediately to college football. These few examples are merely the tip of the iceberg.

POWER PLAY: College football's 25 most powerful people

OP-ED: Federal antitrust protection is only workable path to saving college sports

Eligibility rules have long held a simple purpose: Ensuring a fair playing field while preserving access to the life-changing benefits college sports provide to actual college students. For decades, that standard meant allowing student-athletes four seasons of competition over five years. Recognizing the need for evolution, NCAA member schools recently updated this rule to allow up to five years of competition before age 24. However, since the start of 2025, more than 165 lawsuits have been filed seeking to tear down these basic limits.

As rosters are increasingly packed with older adults and former professionals, the most obvious consequence is an unfair matchup on the field. But the longer-term impact falls on the next generation of young athletes who will be squeezed out of the system as a result. Sidelining incoming freshmen doesn't just rob them of their roster spots or athletic scholarship opportunities — it also strips away their chance to experience the lifelong benefits of college sports. In addition, adding former professionals to rosters costs already-enrolled student-athletes valuable playing time and development opportunities during their precious years in college.

Amid this chaos, the need to pass the Protect College Sports Act is more apparent than ever. This bipartisan bill addresses the current legal instability head-on by creating one clear, fair and enforceable eligibility standard to prevent further erosion of the competitive balance that makes college sports meaningful. Crucially, the PCSA does not stop there. It also codifies important student-athlete benefits into law, including scholarship, healthcare and revenue-sharing protections. And it takes steps to protect broad opportunities, particularly in women's and Olympic sports, by establishing sport minimums and roster protections.

This balanced approach has earned the PCSA a broad consensus of support, uniting professional, Olympic and collegiate sport groups — including student-athlete leaders and conferences across all three divisions — all of whom recognize what's at stake right now for the future of college athletics.

As the Senate prepares to return from recess and the new school year begins, the urgency is higher than ever. College sports matter. They serve our nation's youth, and I believe they are the greatest human development tool in the entire world. By passing the PCSA, lawmakers can ensure they continue to benefit young generations of athletes for decades to come.

Charlie Baker is president of the NCAA.

title: ‘I didn’t want to play very long’ – Joe Burrow addresses potential retirement timeline before season
description: Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow revealed his potential timeline for retirement from the NFL after admitting he never wanted to have a long career. Burrow has been a star in the NFL since entering the league as the No.
fullText:
Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow revealed his potential timeline for retirement from the NFL after admitting he never wanted to have a long career.

Burrow has been a star in the NFL since entering the league as the No. 1 pick in the 2020 NFL Draft. Heading into Year 6, Burrow is regarded as one of the best in his position.

While retirement is definitely not something anyone expects the 29-year-old to do anytime soon, he did speak candidly about what his initial plans were and how he views his career now.

In an interview with Albert Breer, Burrow admitted he wanted to retire early but now feels like he will play until his body does not allow him to do it anymore.

"I used to think I didn't want to play very long, and now I'm like, I'm just going to go until I can't do it anymore. This is fun to do. What the hell else would I do?"

While Tom Brady is an unfair comparison, we did see him play until he was 45 years old. LeBron James is playing a different sport in the NBA, but even he is gearing up to play a 24th season at 42 years old.

Aaron Rodgers is suiting up for his 22nd and final NFL season this year; Aaron Donald just returned from retirement, and even Phillip Rivers returned to the field at 45 years old last season to play for the Colts.

If it's about playing until he physically cannot, Burrow could have well over a decade more to offer fans, barring any catastrophic injury.

It's just a question of how Burrow deals with the inevitable decline in athleticism QBs face in their 30s, and at what level of production he wants to step away from the field.

His decision will also be informed by how, when, or if he wins a Super Bowl in his career. At least Bengals fans can rest assured that their star QB intends to spend more time playing than he initially did.

title: Steelers GM confirms Max Hurleman, Lew Nichols and more practice squad signings
description: The Steelers kept all 10 of their NFL draft picks on the initial 53-man roster, forcing some demotions for some veteran players.
fullText:
More than a dozen players who practiced and played with the Pittsburgh Steelers during training camp and the preseason will be sticking around.

GM Omar Khan confirmed a list of 13 players signed to the team's practice squad as of the afternoon of Monday, Aug. 31.

It includes: Running backs Lew Nichols and Travis Homer; receivers Max Hurleman and Brandon Smith; tight end Lake McRee; offensive linemen Doug Nester and Steven Jones; defensive linemen Esezi Otomewo and Kyler Baugh; cornerback Doneiko Slaughter; safety Sebastian Castro; and linebackers Jacoby Windmon and Julius Welschof.

Required reading: Steelers keep both Drew Allar, Will Howard behind Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph at QB

The Steelers cut all of them from the active roster ahead of the NFL's Sunday deadline to reduce roster sizes to the standard 53 players. The team can still add up to four more names to the practice squad before finalizing the group ahead of Week 1, when they face the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13 at Acrisure Stadium. They will get an exemption for an extra spot because Welschof is an international pathway player.

Nicols and Homer led the backfield in two of three preseason games but were squeezed out of the active roster by rookie Eli Heidenreich, the team's seventh-round selection who also has utility on special teams. He'll be the lone backup behind top backs Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle for now.

Hurleman was a standout with 99 total receiving yards through the three contests against the Green Bay Packers, New York Jets and Buffalo Bills. He gave way to rookie Kaden Wetjen, who's the lead kick returner on special teams, as well as Ben Skowronek, a Pro Bowl selection for his special teams play last season.

McRee opened some eyes working mostly with the backup quarterbacks. He caught a 38-yard pass from Drew Allar in the loss to the Jets on Aug. 21, then added a touchdown from Will Howard in the finale.

Defensively, Welschof had two sacks in the exhibition campaign.

Injuries will be the main factor in any of these players getting called up to the active roster at some point this season. Hurleman, Hurleman and Nichols would be most likely to earn promotions if rookies like Heidenreich and Wetjen struggle to find their footing.

title: British tight end Traore makes Dolphins roster cut
description: British tight end Seydou Traore is included in the Miami Dolphins' initial 53-man roster, meaning he can play from the start of the 2026 NFL season.
fullText:
British tight end Seydou Traore has been included in the Miami Dolphins' initial 53-man roster, meaning he can play from the start of the 2026 NFL season.

The 24-year-old was drafted by the Dolphins in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL Draft in April, becoming the first graduate of England's NFL Academy to complete his pathway to the NFL.

However, despite signing a four-year rookie contract worth $4.8m (£3.6m), he still needed to survive the roster cut from 90 or 91 players to 53.

Traore was born in France but raised in London, where he played for the London Warriors before joining the NFL Academy in 2019.

The academy was set up to help international players earn college scholarships and prepare them for the NFL.

Traore joined Clearwater Academy in Florida before enrolling at Arkansas State University in 2021. He transferred to Mississippi State University in 2023 before entering the draft earlier this year.

His selection in the draft was announced by former NFL defensive end Efe Obada, who also began his journey into American football with the London Warriors.

Meanwhile, Northern Irish kicker Charlie Smyth has been released by the New Orleans Saints after making his NFL debut last season.

title: Seahawks Keep Hard Knocks Fan Favorite on 53-Man Roster
description: A Seahawks Hard Knocks favorite reportedly survived final cuts after going from substitute teaching and real estate back to an NFL roster. The post Seahawks Keep Hard Knocks Fan Favorite on 53-Man Roster appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Seattle Seahawks are officially keeping one of the breakout personalities from their season of HBO's Hard Knocks.

Wide receiver Montorie Foster Jr. has made Seattle's initial 53-man roster,the team announced on Sunday, August 30, as the team worked through its final cuts.

For Foster, making the team would complete one of the more unlikely journeys on Seattle's roster. He went from an undrafted rookie whose first NFL opportunity ended because of injury, to substitute teaching and selling real estate, to becoming one of the players viewers have gotten to know during Hard Knocks.

And unlike many feel-good training camp stories, this one appears to have ended with a roster spot.

Foster's path back to Seattle became a featured storyline during Episode 3 of Hard Knocks.

The Seahawks' official recap noted that Foster spent time with Seattle as an undrafted free agent in 2025 before an injury derailed his first opportunity. After leaving the team, Foster returned home, worked as a substitute teacher and earned his real estate license before eventually getting another opportunity with the Seahawks.

That story continued to get television time as Foster fought for a roster spot.

Gregg Bell of The News Tribune reported that Foster had even substituted at his former high school, St. Edward in Ohio, including an assignment covering a Latin class despite acknowledging he did not know Latin.

His NFL comeback was about more than a television storyline, however.

Foster caught five passes for 36 yards and a touchdown in Seattle's first preseason game, then added receptions of 24 and 13 yards over the Seahawks' final two exhibitions. He finished the preseason with seven catches for 73 yards and a touchdown.

That production gave the Seahawks a football reason to keep him after Hard Knocks gave fans a reason to root for him.

title: J.J. McCarthy Issued Compelling Dolphins Trade Idea Amid Vikings’ Decision

fullText:
On Aug. 30, the Minnesota Vikings announced their 53-man roster for the 2026 NFL season. Moreover, the team's intriguing decision was to go with four QBs, including J.J. McCarthy.McCarthy looks to be QB3 behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz. With Murray and Wentz having an injury history, McCarthy might be an insurance policy in case injuries hit both. However, the Vikings might know that the former first-round pick has some trade value.Any team needing QB help during the season leading up to the trade deadline might call the Vikings over McCarthy. For Mark Powell of FanSided, the Miami Dolphins make sense for the Vikings QB.In an Aug. 30 article, Powell proposed a trade that would see the Dolphins acquire McCarthy in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick. Miami already landed quarterback Kyle McCord in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round draft pick. As a result, Miami probably didn't want to spend much on a backup QB, but if they run into any issues under center, perhaps McCarthy might be an option. "Dumping a former first-round pick is never easy," Powell wrote. "Still, the Dolphins fourth rounder is essentially a late Day 2 pick (since it could very well be the first pick in that round). "The Vikings are a quarterback away from making the postseason, which is why their decision to draft McCarthy, and punt on Kirk Cousins and eventually Sam Darnold, all the more confusing. That is neither here nor there."

As for the Dolphins, they appear content with their two-QB setup for now and will address any issues midseason. Still, Powell argues that someone like McCarthy would be a more reliable option than McCord, who lacks experience in regular-season games. McCord signed with the Packers in January after spending the 2025 season on the Philadelphia Eagles' practice squad after they selected him in the sixth round of last year's draft."Willis is a dual-threat quarterback, which is exciting but also makes him prone to hard contact," Powell added in his article. "Even if Miami intends to tank this season, they'll need someone reliable behind Willis just in case. "I might recommend a veteran backup — which McCarthy is not — but I also wouldn't be tanking as heavily as Jon-Eric Sullivan."

For now, it appears the Dolphins are going with two QBs, but that doesn't mean another team can't call Minnesota for McCarthy. For now, he'll just have to work behind the scenes until an opportunity comes, whether it's in Minnesota or elsewhere.The former Michigan Wolverines product didn't play the preseason finale due to injury, and former NFL player Chad Johnson believes that being injury-prone could be what dooms McCarthy. "I don't know how serious his ankle injury was, but one of the issues that he does have is that he's been injured most of the time since he's been there," Johnson said on the Aug. 28 edition of "Nightcap." "Here we go, we're in the preseason, and you're injured again. "Maybe he thinks his spot is safe. He's one of the few who needs to come in and be playing in a game like this to show that he still has it, because he might be auditioning as well for another team."

title: Green Bay Packers: how being on the commissioner exempt list could affect length of possible Josh Jacobs suspension
description: The Green Bay Packers had a plan for running back throughout the course of the 2026 NFL offseason. Unfortunately, Josh Jacobs getting arrested in May on five charges, including a felony. Obviously, this threw a possible wrench in Green Bay’s plans. Over the course of the last several weeks, there have been rumblings that Jacobs […] The post Green Bay Packers: how being on the commissioner exempt list could affect length of possible Josh Jacobs suspension appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers had a plan for running back throughout the course of the 2026 NFL offseason. Unfortunately, Josh Jacobs getting arrested in May on five charges, including a felony. Obviously, this threw a possible wrench in Green Bay's plans.

Over the course of the last several weeks, there have been rumblings that Jacobs could be suspended by the NFL. This notion gained traction last week when he was formerly charged on two counts. Jacobs was handed down a charge for battery and another for destruction of property. Both of these are misdemeanors.

On Sunday, the day that every NFL team had to trim their rosters from 90 to 53, Roger Goddell decided to place Jacobs on the commissioner's exempt list. While on this list, the Packers running back will continue to collect a paycheck. However, he will not be allowed to practice with the team, play in games, or even step foot in Green Bay football facilities.

Rob Demovsky of ESPN shared the following interpretation of what the collective bargaining agreement says regarding players on the commissioner exempt list:

If my understanding of this is correct, time spent on the commissioner exempt list counts toward a future suspension.

Say if in Week 4, the NFL announces a 6-game suspension for Josh Jacobs, he would only miss 3 more games (but loses 6 games of $).

Correct me if I’m wrong. https://t.co/YX0Akpl8lU

— Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) August 30, 2026

As one can see, the number of games Jacobs spends on the exempt list will count towards the number of games he is potentially suspended. If he is indeed suspended, he will have to forfeit salary to make up for the number of games it is for.

In other words, say he is on the exempt list for the first three games and then is handed a six-game suspension. He would only miss three more games and would not be paid for those games. However, he also will have to forfeit his salary for the first three games.

With Jacobs out, Marshawn Lloyd will be the starting running back in Green Bay. Kaleb Johnson was acquired via trade amid the news from the NFL and will likely serve as the backup. Chris Brooks, who signed a two-year contract earlier this year, will be the third running back on the roster.

The San Francisco 49ers have had quite the offseason, and to put it frankly, they probably (above a lot of other NFL teams) are the most eager to get back on the gridiron to get this 2026 campaign underway.

One development throughout training camp was the Niners sustaining a plethora of injuries to their pass catchers, and the uncertainty of George Kittle's status before Week 1.

Early in training camp, newly signed Christian Kirk sustained a calf injury, which has landed him on Injured Reserve to start the campaign. San Francisco also announced that Isaac Guerendo has landed on the PUP list to begin the season.

As the roster deadline has passed, wide receiver Christian Kirk will begin the 2026 season on the Injured Reserve list with his calf injury, which is now officially more serious than most analysts initially thought.

Christian Kirk (calf) to begin season on IR; will miss at least 4 games.

— Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) August 30, 2026

Kirk will have to miss the first four games of the season, but it's not believed to be a season-ending injury, so Kirk updates will likely be in the future once the season begins.

As for Kirk, it's no surprise that the team will be patient with him. It's one of the benefits of the Injured Reserve. He has experience in ways that Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins do not in the NFL as receivers. Plus, Kirk has production. He will add an element to the passing game the Niners have been missing once he returns.

Christian Kirk is an NFL veteran of eight seasons.

fullText:
I'll keep this one short: The Green Bay Packers target their pre-draft visitors at a high clip, whether it's the draft, as initial undrafted free agents or further down the line. For example, last cutdown cycle the team traded a pick for offensive linemen Darian Kinnard and picked up tight end Josh Whyle to the practice squad. Whyle eventually ended up winning a roster spot and made this year's initial 53-man roster.

So, who was just made available to the Packers? Good question. So far, these are the players who just hit the market and were brought to Green Bay during their draft cycle (since 2022, when the team started targeting more draft picks).

Can I interest anyone in Sean Clifford as a QB3 again?

The one I'm most interested here is rookie Damon Bankston, who received eight times the guarantees to sign with the New York Giants than the Packers' UDFA signing Jaden Nixon got this cycle. If Green Bay is pivoting to a more outside zone-based scheme, which has been the indication, I think Bankston fits really well. With that being said, he would probably be a practice squad signing immediately, not a 53-man roster guy.

I don't think the team wants to go down the Samori Toure path again, but rookie receiver Anthony Smith is interesting. Smith was taken two picks after Packers kicker Trey Smack. The seventh-round pick did not make it on the Dallas Cowboys' roster. He ran a 4.45-second 40-yard dash at 6'2" and 197 pounds.

Both Kiran Amegadjie and Esa Pole are players I could see the Packers adding to the bottom of their offensive line unit. Amegadjie was a third-round pick out of Yale for the Chicago Bears back in 2024, but he never caught on with the team. Esa Pola is a second-year former UDFA who was working with the first-team unit as the team's left tackle in Kansas City at points this summer, but the Chiefs traded for Diego Pounds right before the cutdown deadline.

With seven interior defensive linemen on the 53-man roster, I'm not sure the Packers even need a practice squad defensive lineman right now.

Sam Williams was arrested for felony sexual battery at Ole Miss, but the charges were later dropped. I know now this isn't a great time to say this, but the Packers bring in a lot of prospects with "off-field" red flags for visits, and they generally do it to rule them out completely. I do not expect Williams to be on Green Bay's short list.

Here's an interesting one: Trevin Wallace, the 2024 third-rounder who made 12 starts in 12 games played last year for the Carolina Panthers, was waived by the Panthers today. In total, he played 25 games (20 starts) for Carolina over two regular seasons. I could see the team taking a swing on him.

D'Arco Perkins-McAllister, Chiefs

D'Arco Perkins-McAllister actually started his college career off as a fairly big recruit, but wound up bouncing around schools after two years at TCU. He ended up at New Mexico, UT-Chattanooga and Louisiana-Monroe after that. He was waived by the Kansas City Chiefs, and it's not like the Packers' third-team defensive backs played well in the preseason. Maybe they change things up.

Safety is a position that will probably be more impacted on the practice squad level, if anything, than on the 53-man roster level, but two were made available today. Chris Edmonds has played almost exclusively as a special teamer when he's been active in NFL games in his career, while Jammie Robinson, a former fifth-round pick, is looking to catch on with his sixth team in four years. He's been available before, and the Packers haven't added him, so I'm not sure the 25-year-old is going to be a priority for them now.

fullText:
The Jets have selected the players for their initial roster in 2026. The work is not finished, however.

The team can now begin assembling its practice squad. NFL teams are allowed to assemble a 17 players practice squad. These players practice with the team and attend meetings through the week. Every week, two players can be activated from the practice squad to play in games. These players do not need to be added to the active roster the first three times they are activated for a game. The fourth time, however, the team must add them to the 53 man roster.

Practice squad players are technically free agents and able to sign with the active roster of any team aside from upcoming opponents.

Who is eligible for the practice squad?

Teams can use up to 16 of their 17 slots on players with no NFL seasons or one season (with less than nine games played) if they so choose. For a fully stocked practice squad, the minimum number of players with this level of experience is 6.

Teams are also allowed to choose up to 10 practice squad players with more experience. No more than six can have more than two years of experience in the NFL.

Finally, one spot must go to an international player.

title: Another player involved in college eligibility suit gets cut by an NFL team
description: Defensive lineman Jack Pyburn was waived by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday and could be the latest player who tries to go back to college after spending time in an NFL camp.  Pyburn was among the cuts on the day NFL teams reduced their rosters to 53.
fullText:
Defensive lineman Jack Pyburn was waived by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday and could be the latest player who tries to go back to college after spending time in an NFL camp.

Pyburn was among the cuts on the day NFL teams reduced their rosters to 53. He could now try to get a fifth year of eligibility if he is not claimed on waivers by another team Monday. He'll become a free agent if he's not picked up and is among the players granted a temporary restraining order by a Louisiana court earlier this month that would make them eligible to return to college athletics. Pyburn's likely landing spot would be LSU.

Four other players who spent time on NFL rosters this offseason before being cut were also part of the case: former LSU running back TJ Harden, former Mississippi tight end Dae'Quan Wright, former Ole Miss defensive lineman Zxavian Harris and former Oregon State running back Anthony Hankerson.

These players all entered the NFL draft process because they had used up their four years of eligibility. The NCAA announced a rule change in June allowing players who began college in 2023 or later to have five years to play five seasons.

That rule didn't apply to these players because they entered college in 2022. They have sued the NCAA, arguing they're being deprived of education and potential name, image and likeness benefits by being excluded from the rule.

The Power Four conferences have all ruled that players who signed NFL contracts are ineligible to return to college, but those rules remain in legal limbo until court cases are resolved. The Southeastern Conference's rule is part of a court hearing scheduled for Thursday. SEC rosters become final Friday.

Under NFL rules, any player who returns to college for any time will be ineligible to play this season. Those players would become free agents who are free to sign with any team in 2027.

Here's a look at some of the players who spent time in NFL camps this summer and now might return to college:

Pyburn originally signed as an undrafted free agent with Tampa Bay in May. He played in two exhibition games and led the NFL with four sacks in the preseason. Pyburn played his first three college seasons at Florida and spent last season at LSU.

Harden signed as an undrafted free agent with Cleveland in May before getting waived Aug. 3. He then signed with Seattle three days later and appeared in one exhibition game, gaining 1 yard on two carries and recovering a fumbled punt. He was waived Aug. 17 by the Seahawks. Harden played three years in college at UCLA and finished last season at SMU. He rushed for 2,445 yards and 21 TDs in 44 career games.

Harden is part of the lawsuit in Louisiana and is reportedly interested in playing for Missouri or Kentucky.

Wright originally signed as an undrafted free agent with Philadelphia in the spring but was waived by the Eagles on Aug. 10. He was claimed by Cleveland the next day and spent nearly two weeks with the Browns before getting waived again on Aug. 23. Wright didn't appear in a preseason game. Wright played his first two seasons in college at Virginia Tech and final two at Mississippi. He had 113 catches for 1,603 yards and five TDs in 47 career games.

Wright is part of the lawsuit in Louisiana and wants to play for his former Ole Miss coach, Lane Kiffin, at LSU.

Harris originally signed as an undrafted free agent with New Orleans in May and began training camp with the Saints. He was waived on Aug. 8 before the first preseason game. Harris played four seasons in college at Ole Miss and had 5 1/2 sacks in 52 games. He had two of his career-high nine tackles for loss last season in the College Football Playoff.

Wright is part of the lawsuit in Louisiana and also wants to play for Kiffin at LSU.

Hankerson originally signed as an undrafted free agent with Miami in the spring and began camp with the Dolphins. He was waived on Aug. 10 and signed a week later with Seattle. He spent one week with the Seahawks before getting waived again on Aug. 24. Hankerson had five carries for 10 yards and two catches for 9 yards for Seattle in an exhibition game against Tennessee on Aug. 23. Hankerson played his first two seasons in college at Colorado and the final two at Oregon State. He rushed for 2,761 yards and 28 TDs in 44 career games and had back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons for the Beavers.

Hankerson is part of the lawsuit in Louisiana and could try to return to Oregon State.

title: Ravens waiver-wire priority: Rules, order, and what to know
description: The Ravens hold the No. 14 waiver priority as NFL teams reshape rosters following final roster cuts
fullText:
Constructing the initial 53-man roster is only one stage of the Baltimore Ravens' final preseason evaluation.

The Ravens and the NFL's other 31 teams must reach the 53-player limit by 6 p.m. ET Sunday, Aug. 30. After that deadline, Baltimore can use the waiver wire to pursue young players released elsewhere. Baltimore owns the No. 14 position in the initial waiver order. Thirteen teams will have priority over the Ravens, while Baltimore will sit ahead of 18 other clubs, including the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Pittsburgh Steelers and Philadelphia Eagles.

Players with fewer than four credited NFL seasons are generally required to pass through waivers. Every team may submit a claim, but if multiple organizations pursue the same player, he is awarded to the team with the highest priority.

The Ravens would inherit the player's existing contract and would be required to place him on their active roster. A successful claim could therefore force Baltimore to make another cut or corresponding roster move. Claims on players waived during the final roster reduction must be submitted before 1 p.m. ET Monday, Aug. 31. Teams receive the results simultaneously through the NFL's personnel notice. The system works differently for vested veterans. A player with at least four credited seasons who is released during this portion of the calendar becomes a free agent and can negotiate with any interested team without passing through waivers.

Baltimore's position provides general manager Eric DeCosta with considerably more flexibility than several playoff contenders have. It also does not guarantee the Ravens will land a preferred target if teams near the top of the order become involved. The initial order is based on the final 2025 standings and corresponding 2026 draft order. It will remain unchanged through the first three weekends of the regular season. After that point, waiver priority will reflect the current league standings, with the teams holding the worst records moving to the top.

The Ravens' first 53-man roster should consequently be viewed as a starting point. Injuries, waiver claims and veteran signings could all change its composition before the regular season begins.

title: Kicker Smyth waived by New Orleans Saints

fullText:
Kicker Charlie Smyth has been waived by the New Orleans Saints before the new NFL season.

Smyth, a former Gaelic footballer from Mayobridge in Northern Ireland, was the incumbent coming into pre-season having assumed the role from Blake Grupe in November.

The 25-year-old made 12 of 16 field goals and was successful on each of his 13 extra-point attempts as a starter last season.

But, after a mixed pre-season for Smyth and increased competition on the Saints' kicking roster, two-time All-Pro kicker Daniel Carlson appears to have been given the nod.

In the Saints' final pre-season match against the Dallas Cowboys on Friday, Smyth kicked one extra point but Carlson landed two field goals, including the winning points from 53 yards in the 27-24 victory.

Despite the blow, it does not mean that Smyth's NFL journey has come to an end.

As he came through the NFL's international player pathway (IPP), he could be retained on the Saints' practice roster as IPP players do not count towards the 16-player limit.

He could also become an option for another NFL team if they feel that Smyth could add to their roster.

Teams have until Monday at 17:00 BST to sign released players to their rosters, and from there teams can begin to sign players to their practice squads.

Smyth to have more competition for Saints role

After a fairytale rise to the NFL last year, Smyth was in competition with Carlson and former Louisville Kings kicker Tanner Brown in the off-season as the Saints assessed their kicking options.

Signed to a three-year contract last season, Smyth told BBC NI this month that competition for places in the NFL is "just the way it is in this business" and that he would not be taking any such signings "personally".

Carlson appears to have beaten off competition from Smyth and Tanner Brown, who missed a 39-yard field goal attempt in the pre-season loss to the Los Angeles Rams.

Smyth was also off target from 52 yards in the loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars the previous week.

Carlson, who joined the Saints after those pre-season matches, had his best years in 2021 and 2022, when he was named second-team All-Pro and first-team All-Pro respectively.

He has not missed a game in the past seven seasons but his 81.5% success rate from field goals last year was his lowest since 2019.

The Saints begin their regular season away to the Detroit Lions on 13 September.

The Indianapolis Colts are set with their situation atop their quarterback depth chart. They will be led from under center in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season by Daniel Jones, who has recovered from an Achilles injury he suffered last season in time for the upcoming campaign.

Meanwhile, there still appears to be an ongoing battle for the chief backup role behind Jones, with Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard in the mix.

On Saturday, Richardson and Leonard each had a chance to further make their respective cases for the QB2 job during a real, competitive game, as the Colts faced the visiting Detroit Lions in a preseason finale at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis.

The former Florida Gators star quarterback Richardson started in that game, and he threw for 80 passing yards with zero touchdowns and no interceptions on 7/10 pass completions, while getting sacked for a loss of five yards.

Leonard, on the other hand, went just 3/7 for 48 passing yards with zero touchdowns and was intercepted deep in Lions territory.

Clearly, Richardson had the better outing than Leonard, so it will be interesting how that factors into Indianapolis' final decision on the QB depth order.

Indianapolis head coach Shane Steichen had good words for both Richardson and Leonard despite the latter giving away the ball when the team was on the cusp of scoring.

"I thought Anthony had some good drives, for sure," Steichen said, per the Associated Press (h/t ESPN).

"I think made some good throws, did some good things. I think Riley did some good things as well, just, obviously, don't want to turn it over there in the red zone. But I thought both of them did some good things."

The Colts ended up losing the game to the tune of 25-16 to conclude their preseason winless streak with a 0-2-1 record.

title: NFL waiver wire explained and the Eagles’ position in the claiming order
description: The preseason is almost over and NFL teams have until Sunday, August 30 at 6:00 PM Eastern to get their roster down to just 53 players. 37 players from each team will end up waived or released (if not traded or injury designated), and teams then have an opportunity to put a claim on any […]
fullText:
The preseason is almost over and NFL teams have until Sunday, August 30 at 6:00 PM Eastern to get their roster down to just 53 players.

37 players from each team will end up waived or released (if not traded or injury designated), and teams then have an opportunity to put a claim on any player subject to the waiver wire — and they have until Monday, August 31 at 1:00 to make those decisions. Players claimed will head off to their new teams, and those that pass through unclaimed, will become unrestricted free agents. From there, teams will fill their 16-man practice squads and finalize things heading into Week 1 of the regular season.

Not all players are subject to the waiver wire, however, vested veterans — players who have four years of accrued NFL service time — are outright released. Those players become free agents right away. Teams who are concerned about losing a young player on the waiver wire, might consider releasing a vested veteran on the bubble instead, whom they can bring back immediately on the practice squad, or to the active roster after moving someone else to the scout team.

The Eagles currently sit at the No. 23 spot on the waiver wire, which mirrors the 2026 NFL Draft order. Last year, Howie Roseman claimed center Willie Lampkin, who was waived by the Los Angeles Rams. And Lampkin has been a training camp standout this summer.

The NFL waiver order during the preseason and the first three weeks of the regular season reflects the 2026 NFL Draft order, and then after four games, the order resets to the current league standings. So, right now, the Raiders currently have first pick at every player on waivers. The wire order is also fixed, so the Raiders will get first rights to every single player available regardless of whether they pick one (or many).

fullText:
Detroit's defense intercepted 13 passes last season, tied for 11th in the NFL. Four of those came from cornerbacks, and D.J. Reed accounted for two of them.

Carter Bahns and Zachary Pereles of CBS Sports named the Lions on Thursday among five potential landing spots for New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez, alongside the Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders, New York Giants and Pittsburgh Steelers.

Terrion Arnold, the 24th pick of the 2024 draft, was released by Detroit in June while facing felony charges he has denied, and he agreed to terms with Seattle this month. Reed inherited the No. 1 job, and the group behind him has been shuffled and interrupted by injuries throughout camp.

Tim Twentyman wrote in the club's own training camp position preview in last month that "the Arnold release hurts Detroit's depth at the position," adding it would not surprise him if general manager Brad Holmes added to the spot before the regular season. That went up five weeks before Gonzalez's name entered the conversation, written by someone the team employs.

Detroit ranked 28th in opponent passer rating in the red zone last season at 104.3, allowing 19 passing touchdowns inside its own 20-yard line without intercepting a throw there. Reed's year split around a hamstring strain that cost him six games, and he turns 30 in November.

Gonzalez turned 24 this summer and has two seasons left on his contract. He closed 2025 with three pass breakups and four solo tackles in New England's Super Bowl LX loss to the Seahawks.

The #Lions are listed as a top landing spot for #Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez if he were to be traded Per CBS Sports pic.twitter.com/shw9ae09nF

— NFL Rumors (@nflrums) August 29, 2026

Gonzalez is playing on a rookie deal worth $4.8 million this season that runs through 2027 after New England exercised his fifth-year option in April. Detroit would inherit two years of control and an immediate negotiation, and that negotiation now starts from a number set this month in Seattle, where Devon Witherspoon signed a four-year extension averaging $33 million a season with $101 million in total guarantees and just over $59 million locked in at signing.

The draft compensation would be the cheaper half of the transaction. Bahns and Pereles made that point about the Lions specifically, writing that a long-term deal for Gonzalez would limit Detroit's flexibility at other positions and that the club can carry it only because the money would not take effect until next year.

Robert Kraft said at the start of training camp that New England had offered Gonzalez a deal that would make him the highest-paid cornerback in league history and the highest-paid player in franchise history.

"We love Christian Gonzalez," Kraft said. "We love him as a player, as a person. That's why we've made an offer to him that makes him the highest-paid player ever to play that position in the NFL, and coincidentally, it's the highest contract in the Patriots franchise history,"

Adam Schefter said on The Pat McAfee Show during the week that the sides are "obviously not in the same neighborhood right now and haven't been."

Eliot Wolf, the club's executive vice president of player personnel, answered yes this week when asked if New England still intends to reach that figure.

Gonzalez reported to camp on time and practiced in pads, passing up a holdout that would have cost him $45,000 for every day he missed. He returned to full participation this week after a hard fall on Aug. 10 kept him out of both of the Patriots' first two preseason games. Asked about the standoff, he told reporters it was "frustrating, but I'm focused on the season."

His trainer posted, then deleted, a message on Thursday saying New England should trade him. That remains the loudest anyone in Gonzalez's circle has been all summer.

The Patriots reached Super Bowl LX in February and open this season with a quarterback still on a rookie contract, which places them inside the window where a cornerback of Gonzalez's standing is worth more to them than to anyone else.

title: LSU poised to sign former NFL players after SEC says it will comply with court order
description: Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris are expected to sign with the Tigers.
fullText:
LSU may soon fire the loudest shot yet in a battle with its own conference.

The SEC has communicated to plaintiff attorneys that the league will comply with a Louisiana state court order permitting their clients — former professional football players — from a return to college. Yahoo Sports obtained a message from the conference legal counsel to attorneys signaling the news.

The message paves the way for a host of players to join SEC programs, most notably at LSU, where two players who signed pro contracts this summer are poised to now be on coach Lane Kiffin's roster.

Dae'Quan Wright, the former Ole Miss tight end who signed an undrafted free agent contract with the Cleveland Browns, and Ole Miss defensive tackle Zxavian Harris, who signed with the Saints before being waived, plan to sign with the university. While the signing does not immediately constitute a violation of the SEC's new policy banning former professional players, their inclusion on LSU's final roster would. Rosters are not set until a day before Game 1 (Friday).

The impending signings continues to put at odds the SEC and LSU in an unprecedented legal collision over athlete eligibility that's been brewing for days. A Louisiana judge earlier this month granted Wright and other players an additional year of eligibility through a temporary restraining order by prohibiting the NCAA from enforcing its eligibility standards.

The move created a whirlwind of a week where all the power conferences adopted their own eligibility policy banning pro athletes from returning to college. And then, on Friday, a Baton Rouge judge granted a request from players' attorneys to also enjoin the SEC's new rule, amending the complaint to add the league and commissioner Greg Sankey as defendants.

It's not only football. RJ Luis, a basketball standout who played three games in the NBA and was part of two franchises, is a commitment to Will Wade's hoops team.

The addition of all three players violated two SEC policies: the ban on pro players and the prohibition on players moving from one conference member to another outside of the transfer portal window. Each violation comes with stiff sanctions, including a half-season suspension of the head coach, a 50% fine of a school's athletic budget and the forfeiture of voting privileges.

However, the Louisiana judge's order prohibits the league from enforcing sanctions against a school, coach or athlete. A preliminary injunction hearing - where the judge determines if the restraining order will be more permanent until a trial - is scheduled for Thursday in Baton Rouge.

Two days later, LSU hosts Clemson in a top-25 game in Tiger Stadium in coach Lane Kiffin's debut.

The Tigers aren't necessarily alone in intentionally leaving open roster spots for pro players and/or those transferring within the league outside of the portal window. Texas has a player, Cole Hutson, who participated in mini camp with two NFL teams, received a state injunction and is practicing with the Longhorns. Kentucky is expected to sign former Missouri players Mark Mitchell, who played games in the NBA summer league.

But the Tigers have been the most aggressive, with their brash coach and even the Louisiana governor leading the way.

In a news conference on Monday, Kiffin said the players suing the NCA were "wronged" because of the association's timing of the new eligibility policy, suggested that other programs are also recruiting the same athletes and said he's only trying to improve his roster through a "relentless pursuit of excellence."

"That's how I live," he said. "It's how I run the team. And that we're always going to look at every avenue to give you the best team, to give you the best players, so that you have the best chance to win."

The state's governor, Jeff Landry, released a statement to Front Office Sports earlier this week on the issue, blaming the system and not his state school: "Don't hate the player; hate the game."

More players are available outside of the Louisiana suit.

A Dallas judge on Thursday granted additional eligibility to more than two dozen athletes playing multiple sports - a complaint filed, like the Louisiana one, by attorney Ryan Downton and the Texas Trial Lawyers. Downton represented former Vanderbilt quarterback Diego Pavia in a case in 2024 that opened the floodgates for many eligibility lawsuits against the association.

But the latest wave of cases stems from the NCAA's new eligibility policy enacted this summer. The new rule grants athletes five seasons of eligibility, up from four under the previous bylaw. The association chose not to make an exception for players graduating this spring who exhausted their eligibility under the former policy.

That decision, made by the member schools themselves, sparked the current landscape: more than 300 athletes filing 60-plus lawsuits for an additional year, including those who this spring signed pro contracts without knowledge of the NCAA's rule change. Athletes have won a wide portion of those rulings, but inconsistent judicial decisions - the NCAA has, for now, won cases in Ohio, New York, Nevada and a federal suit in Colorado - has created an uneven competitive playing field.

"The 'chaos' of NFL players going back to college is a one-time occurrence specifically resulting from the NCAA arbitrarily denying Class of 2022 athletes from having a fifth year under its new rule, which the NCAA forecasted was coming for a long time," Florida based sports lawyer Darren Heitner, who's assisting with the lawsuit and represents some of the players involved, posted online earlier this week.

"They wouldn't have been NFL players at all if the NCAA would have rightfully given them an extra year. Alternatively, had the NCAA provided the option of a fifth year and the athlete still went to the NFL, the player wouldn't be allowed to go back to college. But that's not what happened."

Judges are not only granting athletes eligibility but creating temporary windows for them to transfer and permitting pro players to return to college - a long-honored college policy that is now under attack, in part because of the monetary incentive. Pro athletes cut from rosters are expected to receive big pay days at their colleges through NIL and revenue-share agreements.

The act of schools accepting professional players is emerging as a seminal moment in the industry, as college executives rally to halt the action. Within a matter of 48 hours, leaders of the Big Ten, SEC, Big 12 and ACC adopted their own pro-player bans in an effort to evade legal challenges by governing a smaller group of schools than the hundreds under the NCAA umbrella. But despite unanimous votes from school presidents to pass such rules, universities are leaving open roster spots and are, privately, supporting players in legal battles - most notably LSU, which played a role in the Louisiana filing.

The situation has sprung to life the industry and its legion of fans - many of whom do not publicly support the return of pro athletes.

College Football Playoff leaders may soon follow the power leagues, in fact. They plan next week to seriously discuss and possibly adopt a participation policy that disqualifies several categories of athletes, including those who have previously signed pro contracts, sources with knowledge of the talks told Yahoo Sports.

But plaintiff attorneys believe that these athletes belonging to the 2022 high school class should have been granted an additional year of eligibility. On the other side, NCAA and conference officials believe they are taking spots from other players on the eve of the start of the fall sports season.

"Courts across the country granting relief to ineligible athletes who already had every opportunity to compete in college - sometimes without even having a hearing - are failing to appreciate the destabilizing effect their rulings are having on college sports," the NCAA released in a statement earlier this month. "The lawyers bringing these cases seemingly won't be satisfied until every professional athlete can treat college sports as a fallback option, regardless of the opportunities it strips from both those who will never have a chance to begin their collegiate sports experience and those who are currently on campus working out with the team and attending classes."

title: You’re going to see some absurdly long field goals in the NFL this season. Here’s why
description: Last season, Jacksonville Jaguars kicker Cam Little drilled a 68-yard field goal that became the longest field goal ever made in an NFL game. That kick was actually shorter than the 70-yarder he hit during the preseason. Then, just last week, Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker hit a 69-yarder of his own. Absurdly long…
fullText:
Last season, Jacksonville Jaguars kicker Cam Little drilled a 68-yard field goal that became the longest field goal ever made in an NFL game. That kick was actually shorter than the 70-yarder he hit during the preseason. Then, just last week, Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker hit a 69-yarder of his own.

Absurdly long field goals are becoming a pattern in the NFL, and it's almost surely going to continue this year.

Over the past few seasons, the NFL has quietly made some changes to its kicking balls that seem to have made things noticeably easier on kickers. That, coupled with the recent kickoff changes that have made a drastic impact on starting field position, has led to an increase in incredibly long field goals.

Ahead of the 2025 season, the NFL quietly passed a resolution that allowed teams to prepare their kicking balls – known in the league as "K-balls" – before game day, rather than during game day. The change got very little publicity, likely because nobody really expected the change to make a drastic difference. But it seems to have, and Philadelphia Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio took notice.

Following a game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in which kicker Chase McLaughlin hit a 65-yard field goal and a 58-yard field goal, Fangio brought up the quiet rule change, saying that it made a "drastic" impact on the kicking game. Fangio said the impact has been so drastic that he compared it to the steroid era of Major League Baseball.

"You know what you guys have missed? Not just you but everybody is, we gave up a 65-yard field goal and a 58-yard field goal," he told reporters via ESPN. "These kicking balls that changed this year, have drastically changed the kicking game, field goals in particular. It's almost like they need an asterisk era, like it was the live ball era, or the asterisk for those home runs that [Barry] Bonds or [Sammy] Sosa or [Mark] McGwire were hitting. The way they have changed the ball, the NFL has drastically changed the field goals."

The new rules allow teams to break in the balls throughout the week rather than just in the minutes leading up to the game, which allows for the ball to fly a bit further, anonymous special teams coordinators told ESPN.

"The ball is flying 5 yards further because the balls are broken in well," an anonymous special teams coordinator told ESPN in a text message.

The data doesn't lie, either. In 2024, kickers made just four of 14 attempts beyond 60 yards – just 29%. In 2025, that number jumped to 12 of 22 – 55%. And it sounds like the league is happy with those results, especially when it leads to exciting, game-ending long field goals.

"After four weeks, I've walked out of here at the Art McNally Gameday Central, like, damn, we had three walk-off field goals today!" NFL executive vice president of football operations Troy Vincent said. "And it's not just walk-off. They're not like they are 30 yards, they are kicking that thing from 50-plus, and they're walking off."

While the new rules for the kicking balls have seemingly made it easier for kickers to connect from long distances, the new kickoff rules will likely give them more opportunities.

Beginning in 2024, the NFL moved to its new dynamic kickoff format. While the league said that the new kickoff format was designed to increase the number of kickoff returns while minimizing the number of high-speed collisions, the change has also had another consequence: a drastic improvement in starting field position.

Under the new format, a touchback results in the offense taking possession at the 35-yard line, up 10 yards from the 25-yard line. Additionally, the new kickoff format has produced some longer returns on average. As a result, the average starting field position is up dramatically, from the 25.6-yard line to the 30.6-yard line.

That's obviously had an impact on scoring, as better starting field position leads to more scoring opportunities. It also has the potential to increase long field goals.

The NFL has no shortage of kickers who can reliably connect from long range – guys like Little, Butker, McLaughlin, Evan McPherson, Brandon Aubrey, just to name a few. If the range for those players is now on their own side of the field thanks to the new kicking balls, offenses are now just a play or two away from field goal range before they even step onto the field, thanks to the new kickoff format.

As teams and kickers gradually realize that field goal range is longer than it's ever been and they have more chances at these long kicks than ever before, expect to see a drastic increase in absurdly long field goal attempts this season and beyond.

title: Penix Closes Gap as Falcons QB Race Boils Over
description: The gap Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa has been closed in the Atlanta Falcons quarterback race, according to Yahoo Sports . NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport says the lead Tagovailoa held is gone. Both players will now split first-team reps to settle the starting job. The competition is wide open and the pressure is…
fullText:
The gap Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa has been closed in the Atlanta Falcons quarterback race, according to Yahoo Sports. NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport says the lead Tagovailoa held is gone. Both players will now split first-team reps to settle the starting job. The competition is wide open and the pressure is on for both men.

Tagovailoa started with a huge advantage. He looked great during the offseason while Penix was stuck on the sideline. The organization wanted him to win the job and move forward as the starter. That plan relied on Penix staying injured for a while. But the knee injury healed faster than expected.

Penix needed surgery in the week of November 24, 2025, to address a partially torn ACL in his left knee. Before that hurt knee, he threw for 1,982 yards. He completed 60.1 per cent of his passes. Nine total touchdowns and three interceptions were recorded by him during the 2025 season. Now he is back and ready to fight.

Tagovailoa has not looked as sharp in the preseason. Both in practice and in games, Rapoport noted that he had been inconsistent. The gap that seemed so wide has shrunk to nothing. Rapoport explained that Tagovailoa 'had a big-time lead in this race'. That lead is under serious pressure now.

Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski confirmed the split reps. This move proves the door is open for Penix. Rapoport stated that while he seems to have been practicing better the last couple of days, the door is open for Michael Penix. That quote from Rapoport sums up the whole situation perfectly.

The coach made the call after Penix was cleared for 11-on-11 work. This means the competition can now properly begin. Both players get to show what they can do on the field. No more waiting for the injured guy to catch up. They are both in the mix right now.

Penix knows what he can do. He told reporters that as far as a pocket, he can do everything. He is confident in his skills. The only thing holding him back is his doctor's advice on taking hits. His doctor is still waiting for the point when he is comfortable with him taking hits.

That time is getting closer every day. The Falcons' quarterback decision could soon become much clearer. Fans will see the real difference between these two soon enough. The split reps are the first step in a long battle.

There is plenty at stake for Tagovailoa. He is on a one-year deal. This game could be his only chance to prove he belongs. If he loses the job, he might not have another shot in Atlanta. He needs to show he is the long-term starter in the NFL.

Penix faces his own pressure too. He spent much of training camp working his way back. He cannot afford to waste this opportunity. He needs to reclaim the starting role he appeared set to compete for before his injury. The clock is ticking for both of them.

The original plan was for Penix to rehab his knee and return when healthy. The team hoped he would just give Atlanta another option if a change was needed during the season. Now that plan is dead. The team has to pick one man to lead the offense.

Tagovailoa has struggled during the preseason. Rapoport noted that he had been inconsistent both in practice and in games. The door is open for Michael Penix to walk right in. The Falcons fans will get their answer very soon. The race has reached a boiling point.

fullText:
From four wins to the NFC Championship Game was one of the most remarkable turnarounds in recent NFL history. But the Washington Commanders have suffered a hard reset since a thrilling rookie season for Jayden Daniels.

After a disastrous 2025 campaign, the team had to hope for a bounce back this season. But the summer has been far from perfect, leaving a few analysts worried about how the team will fare this year.

Last season, with Daniels playing in just seven games, the team quickly fell apart, with an eight-game losing streak effectively ending their year before it even truly began. As a result, they finished with a 5-12 record.

The defense, which ranked second-to-last on PFN's Defense Impact Metric, and the offensive line, which ranked 19th on PFN's Team Offensive Line Impact Metrics, were among the biggest problems for the Commanders last season.

title: Ex-Raiders RB Faces Criminal Charges as Potential NFL Suspension Looms

fullText:
Former Las Vegas Raiders running back Josh Jacobs has been formally charged after an alleged domestic violence incident at his home in May.

Jacobs was initially accused of grabbing the arm of a woman identified as his girlfriend during a struggle in their home. He was charged on Thursday by prosecutors in Wisconsin, facing two misdemeanor charges related to the incident.

As ESPN reported, Jacobs was charged with misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property.

"Our office sought to ensure a fair and complete review of available evidence, some of which only recently became available to our office due to significant, ongoing forensic efforts by law enforcement," Brown County District Attorney David L. Lasee said in a statement. "A criminal complaint is nothing more than a written, formal accusation against a defendant alleging the commission of criminal offenses and does not raise any inference of guilt. Mr. Jacobs is presumed innocent of these charges. As this is an ongoing criminal case, and out of respect for the rights of all parties, our office will not have further comment on the matter at this time."

Jacobs could risk nine months in prison and a fine of up to $10,000 for each charge if convicted.

The running back's lawyers released a statement noting that police did not formally charge him with domestic violence.

"The Brown County District Attorney has reviewed evidence and elected to file misdemeanor charges against Josh that do not include domestic violence," noted the lawyers, David Z. Chesnoff, Richard A. Schonfeld and Clarence F. Duchac III. "The allegations will be addressed in court, and not in the media. Mr. Jacobs respects the District Attorney's office and the process it followed."

Jacobs started his NFL career with the Raiders in 2019 and had success as the team's running back, leading the NFL in 2022 with 1,653 rushing yards. He joined the Packers in 2024.

Jacobs is set to make a court appearance on Nov. 17.

As ESPN noted, the league is investigating the allegations and could suspend Jacobs either to start the season or once his court case has concluded. The league has wide latitude to issue punishment in cases of alleged domestic violence, even if charges are ultimately dropped.

The Packers said they would continue to cooperate with the NFL during the investigation, but would not comment further on the charges.

title: European franchise a question for NFL - Belichick
description: Six-time Super Bowl winning head coach Bill Belichick says the possibility of a European franchise is a question for the NFL.
fullText:
Six-time Super Bowl winning head coach Bill Belichick says the possibility of a European franchise is a question for the NFL, but welcomes the global expansion of American football.

NFL fixtures regularly take place across Europe throughout the season and there also has an international pathway for players, but all 32 franchises are in the United States.

Belichick was speaking in Dublin before the American College Classic on Saturday (17:00 BST) between his North Carolina Tar Heels side and the Texas Christian University, which is the opening round of the season.

The 74-year-old - regarded as one of the greatest coaches of all time - took over as head coach of UNC in 2025 after a glittering 23 years with the New England Patriots in the NFL, where he won six Super Bowls.

When asked if he felt a European franchise was feasible or if it was something he would want to see happen, Belichick said it was "a question for the NFL and commissioner [Roger] Goodell".

"The NFL is very intent on building a global brand and you can see that in their scheduling this year," he said.

"Every time I've been part of those international games, the enthusiasm and the excitement is tremendous.

"I'm sure the NFL will continue to pursue that. College football is doing it with this game, so I think it is great for the game."

Belichick 'wisdom' guiding UNC on Dublin trip

Belichick highlighted that the possibility of the Jacksonville Jaguars relocating to London and Wembley had been explored in the past, but they ultimately stayed put and built their own new stadium in Florida.

He did, however, believe the travel involved would not stop a franchise being developed in Europe.

"It would certainly be a little bit of an adjustment coming here, but it's not a whole lot different than coming from the east coast to the west coast in the USA," Belichick added.

"Time-wise it's a long trip, but going from New York or Boston or Philly to LA or Seattle, it's about the same."

After 23 years in the NFL, Belichick said it was "important" for him to give back to the sport that "has been good to me and my family".

"American football is a great game, fans around the world love it.

"There's not a lot of it being played outside of the US, but I know when I visited places like Croatia or Germany there are a lot of local teams who play in their own leagues.

"It's super-popular. Anything I can do to give back to the game, whether that is in our country or internationally, I want to be part of that and I want to do it."

When asked if he would ever return to the NFL in a coaching capacity, Belichick said his full focus was on North Carolina.

"I recruited these kids and I want to help them," he added.

"I had a great experience in the NFL but I'm very happy to be at North Carolina and I'm excited about the future of our programme."

title: Super Bowl champions Seahawks to be sold in record $9.6bn deal
description: NFL owners approve the $9.612bn record sale of the reigning Super Bowl champions Seattle Seahawks to a group led by billionaire Vinod Khosla.
fullText:
NFL owners have approved the $9.612bn record sale of the reigning Super Bowl champions Seattle Seahawks to a group led by billionaire Vinod Khosla.

The deal, which required the support of at least 24 of 32 owners, is currently the second highest amount paid for a franchise in North American sports history.

The estate of Paul G. Allen, which inherited the NFL team after the death of the Microsoft co-founder in 2018, agreed to terms with the Khosla family on 11 July after a search for a new owner.

And now approved, the sale surpasses the $6.05bn the Washington Commanders fetched when they were sold in 2023, although the NBA's Los Angeles Lakers were subsequently sold for $10bn in 2025 and are currently in the process of changing ownership again for a reported $12.5bn.

"We are honoured to be entrusted as the next stewards of the Seattle Seahawks. How often do you get to buy a franchise that just won the Super Bowl?" said Khosla.

"We are incredibly lucky and humbled by this gift, I would say, from the Allen trust."

"We look forward to building on the winning legacy Paul Allen created and to earning the trust of the Seahawks organisation and fans everywhere."

Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday, Khosla, who will have to relinquish a minority stake in the San Francisco 49ers as part of his agreement to buy the Seahawks, added: "The task ahead is actually pretty simple - keep the winning streak alive, get another Super Bowl.

"Our approach is generally going to be long-term focused, that's our inclination always. So, keep winning, take a long-term approach, and learn a lot. We don't know enough, and the other owners have been incredibly welcoming and willing to teach us, so we'll learn a lot.

"We'll learn from management and see what they are recommending."

Khosla, 71, was the co-founder of US technology company Sun Microsystems and the founder of the venture capital firm Khosla Ventures and has a net worth of $13.2bn, according to Forbes. , external

Former owner Allen saved the Seahawks from relocating to Southern California when he bought the team from Ken Behring in 1997.

His sister, Jody Allen, took control of the Seahawks and the NBA's Portland Trail Blazers as chair of both teams upon her brother's death with a directive to eventually sell both and donate the proceeds to charity.

In the 29 seasons in which Paul or Jody Allen were in charge, the Seahawks made the play-offs 17 times and won two of the four Super Bowls they contested.
